tracks.name: Foundations & Futures Market Mechanics
tracks.description: Identify the listed instrument, expiry, data series, exchange terms and tick arithmetic before using ICT concepts.
completionCriteria: Identify the exchange, root, expiry and chart-series mapping.
Find the current primary contract specification.
Calculate hypothetical tick risk with fees stated separately.

tracks.name: Market Structure & Dealing Ranges
tracks.description: Build directional context from confirmed swings, structure breaks, displacement and a consistently declared dealing range.
completionCriteria: Define swing and close rules before marking.
Classify BOS/MSS without changing thresholds after the event.
Map the dealing range and midpoint reproducibly.

tracks.name: Liquidity & Draw on Liquidity
tracks.description: Map internal/external liquidity and distinguish a sweep from accepted continuation.
completionCriteria: Map BSL/SSL and prior/session reference levels with time definitions.
Separate sweep/raid from a liquidity run using a written rule.
Record the intended draw, invalidation and no-trade case.

tracks.name: Displacement & Imbalances
tracks.description: Define displacement and measure gaps/imbalances with explicit boundary and mitigation conventions.
completionCriteria: Define displacement and imbalance criteria in testable terms.
Record wick/close and mitigation rules.
Reject an isolated gap without the setup preconditions.

tracks.name: PD Arrays: FVG, OB, Breaker & Related Zones
tracks.description: Compare PD arrays, their boundaries, thresholds, definition variants, overlap and invalidation.
completionCriteria: State the exact definition used and its evidence label.
Mark boundaries and invalidation using a repeatable rule.
Separate original/source-described terms from conventions.

tracks.name: Time, Sessions & Daily/Weekly Narratives
tracks.description: Use time anchors, sessions and narrative models without mistaking a timing window for an entry trigger.
completionCriteria: Store time windows with an IANA timezone and DST handling.
Differentiate a timing window from an entry trigger.
Label community and synthesis conventions.

tracks.name: Entry Models & Execution Checklists
tracks.description: Combine prerequisites into explicit setup sequence, execution assumptions, stops, targets and no-trade rules.
completionCriteria: Write the full precondition-to-invalidation sequence.
Specify order type and fill assumptions without suggesting execution.
Avoid performance claims without linked reproducible tests.

tracks.name: Cross-Market Futures SMT & Confirmation
tracks.description: Compare aligned futures contracts, expiries and swing times with explicit composition and correlation caveats.
completionCriteria: Use aligned expiry and synchronised comparison times.
Distinguish PDF-listed SMT pairs from other compare conventions.
Record event/correlation reasons that may explain divergence.

tracks.name: Futures Contracts, Roll & Risk Application
tracks.description: Apply expiry, continuous mapping, margin, position risk and volume/OI concepts to listed futures.
completionCriteria: Verify active expiry and first-notice/delivery rules when relevant.
Explain roll mapping and validate chart events against expiry-specific data.
Calculate stop risk with current tick values and explicit costs.

tracks.name: Replay, Journaling & Evidence-Based Model Evaluation
tracks.description: Turn lesson concepts into dated replay tasks, source-aware journals and no-hindsight evaluation.
completionCriteria: Complete relevant replay tutorial with contract, expiry, timeframe, timezone and source metadata.
Keep a written rule and rejected/no-trade examples.
Use TESTED only with reproducible costs, sample size and out-of-sample evidence.

concepts.name: Market Structure
concepts.definition: Framework for reading swing highs, swing lows and directional sequences. The playbook uses higher-timeframe structure for context before lower-timeframe execution.
howToUse: Mark meaningful confirmed Monthly/Weekly/Daily swings.
Identify the latest structural break and displacement leg.
Use 4H/1H to refine context; do not let a 1M fluctuation redefine daily bias.
concepts.useCase: Use a pre-defined swing-selection rule and keep it consistent.
concepts.commonMistakes: Swing selection is discretionary unless the lookback and close rule are specified.
concepts.youtubeQuery: Inner Circle Trader official Market Structure ICT futures
concepts.sourceNote: The supplied PDF is the source for playbook framing where explicitly marked. Supplemental clarifications are identified as such. These are discovery links, not verified video-to-concept mappings.

learningObjectives: Explain Market Structure in your own words and state what chart observation qualifies.
Apply the concept using a fixed timeframe, source and wick/body or session rule where relevant.
Record the evidence, invalidation, alternative explanation and a no-trade case without hindsight edits.

workedExample.title: Hypothetical swing-break review
workedExample.body: On a fictional 5-minute ES chart, a confirmed swing high is 5,200.00. Price trades to 5,202.00 but closes at 5,199.50. If your written BOS rule requires a candle-body close beyond the swing, this is not a confirmed BOS. If a later candle closes at 5,203.00 with a pre-defined displacement condition, log that later event separately.

checklist: Record instrument/contract, expiry convention, chart timeframe, data source, date and timezone.

Record invalidation, an alternative interpretation and at least one rejected/no-trade example.
practicalExercise.deliverable: A dated screenshot or chart pack plus a short rule sheet. The work is considered complete when a second person can reproduce the classification from the recorded rules.
reviewCriteria: The rule was written before outcome review.
The chart evidence matches the rule and includes timestamp/timeframe.
Invalidation and disqualified cases are documented.

Treat the label as a guaranteed market mechanism.
Change the definition after the outcome is known.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: A research term should be defined, sourced and measured consistently. Avoid treating model language as proof of causation or edge.
knowledgeCheck.correctAnswer: Mark meaningful confirmed Monthly/Weekly/Daily swings.

concepts.definition: A break of a prior structural swing in the direction of the existing trend. It is a continuation clue, not an automatic entry.
howToUse: Define the swing level before the break.
Decide whether a wick or candle-body close qualifies.
Check displacement and the next liquidity pool.

concepts.definition: A break through a relevant swing opposite to prior short-term structure, ideally with displacement. In the playbook, MSS confirms after a liquidity raid.

concepts.name: Liquidity
concepts.definition: In ICT terminology, liquidity refers to orders or stops thought to cluster around obvious highs, lows and reference levels. The playbook uses pools to frame draw on liquidity.
howToUse: Mark prior highs/lows, equal highs/lows and session extremes.
Separate target pool from trigger.
Ask which untouched external level aligns with higher-timeframe narrative.
concepts.useCase: Use as a map of potential objectives, not proof that stops are visible or guaranteed to be taken.
concepts.commonMistakes: Do not assume every equal high/low must be swept.

learningObjectives: Explain Liquidity in your own words and state what chart observation qualifies.

concepts.name: Fair Value Gap (FVG)

howToUse: Identify first and third candles.

Mark 50% CE if used.
Define wick-touch versus body-close mitigation/invalidation.

concepts.commonMistakes: The PDF reports no robust proof that FVGs outperform equal-sized random zones; fills are not guaranteed.

concepts.name: Premium & Discount
concepts.definition: Within a defined dealing range, above the 50% equilibrium is premium and below is discount. The PDF advises using a range formed by a meaningful structural event.
howToUse: Select structural swing low/high.
Mark 50% equilibrium.
Classify upper/lower half.
Do not redraw range after outcome.
concepts.useCase: Directional filter: longs often sought in discount and shorts in premium with other confirmation.
concepts.commonMistakes: Cheap/expensive is relative to chosen range and does not guarantee reversal.

concepts.name: Change in State of Delivery (CISD)
concepts.definition: A short-term delivery-change label used when price closes through a chosen opening-price reference from a prior directional candle run. It is a defined close/open observation, not proof of institutional intent.
howToUse: Define the directional candle run and its reference open before reviewing the setup.
For a bullish read, require a candle body close above the chosen bearish-run reference open; for a bearish read, require a body close below the chosen bullish-run reference open.
Record separately whether price also breaks a selected swing; CISD and MSS are not automatically interchangeable.
Predefine invalidation and the next liquidity objective.
concepts.useCase: Use as a lower-timeframe delivery-shift observation alongside higher-timeframe location and liquidity.
concepts.commonMistakes: Different educators choose the anchor candle differently. A wick through the level is not a body-close confirmation under the common rule. No audited predictive win rate is established.

concepts.name: Market Maker Model (MMXM)
concepts.definition: A broad campaign narrative describing price moving away from an origin range in stages, reaching a higher-timeframe reference area, and potentially reversing through prior ranges or pauses. The wording does not prove the actual orders or intentions of a market maker.
howToUse: Mark the original consolidation or dealing range.
Map the first directional leg and intermediate consolidations as price moves away from the origin.
Identify a higher-timeframe reference area where a reversal would need separate confirmation.
Only map the next leg after a clear structure/delivery shift; mark invalidation and opposing liquidity.
concepts.useCase: Use as a multi-leg narrative map during historical chart study, not as an intraday trigger by itself.
concepts.commonMistakes: Retrofitting every chart into a buy/sell campaign; treating “market maker” language as evidence of a specific institution; assuming the entire path must complete.

howToUse: First identify a valid order block created by displacement.

concepts.name: Breakaway Gap
concepts.definition: A label found in some secondary ICT/SMC references for an imbalance left behind during a decisive move that does not promptly rebalance. It should not be confused with an exchange-session opening gap.
howToUse: Identify the exact imbalance boundaries using the source-specific definition.
Record the impulse leg and the session in which it formed.
Track whether price retraces, partially mitigates or leaves the zone open.
Keep continuous-contract rollover gaps and session-opening gaps distinct from three-candle FVGs.
concepts.useCase: Use as a descriptive label for an abandoned imbalance only when the chosen source defines it precisely.
concepts.commonMistakes: Treating every chart gap as an ICT FVG; confusing roll gaps, NDOG/NWOG and candle-formation imbalances.

concepts.name: Inversion FVG (IFVG) Reversal Model
concepts.definition: The supplied playbook defines an IFVG when price body-closes through the far boundary of an existing FVG, changing its role. A retest entry is a further model convention.
howToUse: Mark the original bullish or bearish FVG and record its direction.
Wait for a body close through the far boundary; a wick alone does not qualify under the playbook rule.
Mark the inverse support/resistance role and wait for a retest if that is the written plan.
Set invalidation beyond the inverted zone and target the next opposing liquidity.

concepts.name: Futures Expiry, First Notice & Roll

howToUse: Calculate stop risk from current tick value
check current initial/maintenance margin and broker add-ons separately
include commission, slippage and tail risk.

concepts.name: Futures Volume, Open Interest & COT
concepts.definition: Exchange volume counts traded contracts in an interval; open interest counts outstanding open contracts at a reporting time; CFTC COT classifies aggregate positions at a report cadence. They are distinct measures and cannot replace each other or order-book depth.
howToUse: Label source, market, contract month, observation period, report date and retrieval time
compare only aligned measures.
concepts.useCase: Use exchange volume/OI for activity, COT for reported trader-category positions and report frequency from current official schedules.
concepts.commonMistakes: Calling weekly COT intraday flow; treating open interest as volume; inferring buy/sell direction from volume alone.

tutorials.title: Build a Higher-Timeframe Structure Map
tutorials.objective: Create a repeatable structure map using confirmed swings, continuation breaks and potential shifts.
materials: One completed futures chart with at least Daily, 1H and 5M views
A written swing and candle-close rule
A replay or screenshot tool
steps: Choose one instrument and one completed date. Record the contract/continuous symbol, expiry convention, chart feed and timezone.
On Daily and 1H, mark only swings that satisfy one preselected pivot rule. Do not use a future-known turning point before it is confirmed.
Identify the latest relevant break. Label BOS only when the predeclared level and wick/body rule are met.
If studying a possible reversal, record the prior short-term swing, the opposing break and whether displacement accompanies it. Keep MSS distinct from a continuation BOS.
Move to 5M only after the higher-timeframe map is saved. Record what lower-timeframe information refines the map and what does not change it.
tutorials.deliverable: A three-timeframe chart pack with five annotated pivots, one candidate BOS/MSS decision and a written invalidation/no-trade note.
review: Pivot rule is stated before marking.
BOS and MSS are not used interchangeably.
The lower timeframe does not retroactively rewrite the higher-timeframe swing map.
tutorials.sourceNotes: Practice workflow based on the playbook; completion is educational practice, not evidence of strategy performance.

tutorials.title: Create a Liquidity Reference Ledger
tutorials.objective: Map potential buy-side/sell-side objectives and distinguish a reference level from an entry trigger.
materials: A completed NQ, ES, GC or CL session chart
A fixed definition of trading day/week and session timezone
A spreadsheet or journal
steps: Before reviewing the outcome, record the product, expiry, data feed, timezone and session definition.
Mark the last completed day and week highs/lows, plus the chosen session high/low.
Mark equal-high/equal-low clusters using a tolerance fixed in ticks or points before reviewing the move.
Label potential BSL above highs and SSL below lows. Describe these as chart-based hypotheses, not visible orders or measured resting liquidity.
Choose one possible opposing pool as an objective and record what separate trigger would be required before a trade could be considered.
tutorials.deliverable: A dated liquidity ledger with at least six premarked pools, tolerance/session rules and a separate trigger column.
review: Levels were marked before studying the later move.
Exchange trading day is not confused with calendar midnight.
No assumption that every pool must be taken.
tutorials.sourceNotes: Practice workflow based on the playbook; completion is educational practice, not evidence of strategy performance.

tutorials.title: Separate a Liquidity Sweep from Breakout Acceptance
tutorials.objective: Classify level interactions using a consistent reclaim/acceptance rule instead of hindsight labels.
materials: At least ten completed level interactions
A chosen wick/body close rule
A chart replay tool
steps: Select ten prior-day, prior-week, equal-high/low or session levels and mark them before replay.
For every interaction, record whether price traded beyond the level, reclaimed it, closed back inside, or held outside with follow-through.
Apply the same close and confirmation rule to all ten cases. Do not rename a failed breakout after seeing the eventual direction.
For a potential reversal, require the additional trigger specified by the chosen playbook (for example displacement and a selected structure break); the sweep itself is not an entry.
Record ambiguous cases as ambiguous rather than forcing a sweep/run label.
tutorials.deliverable: A ten-case classification sheet with screenshots, timestamps, reclaim/acceptance labels and separate trigger outcomes.
review: The reclaim/acceptance rule is fixed in advance.
A wick through a level is not automatically a reversal.
Ambiguous observations are retained.
tutorials.sourceNotes: Practice workflow based on the playbook; completion is educational practice, not evidence of strategy performance.

tutorials.title: Measure FVGs, CE, IFVG and BPR
tutorials.objective: Measure three-candle FVGs and related imbalance concepts with exact boundaries and explicit invalidation rules.
materials: OHLC candles on one named timeframe
A calculator or chart measurement tool
A written wick/body mitigation rule
steps: Choose one timeframe and write down whether the data are time-based or trade-based. Use the candle highs/lows, not a drawn box alone.
For a bullish FVG, check whether candle 3 low is above candle 1 high; for a bearish FVG, check whether candle 3 high is below candle 1 low.
Record each gap's far edges and calculate its midpoint (CE) arithmetically. Do not assume the midpoint causes a reaction.
If studying IFVG, require the source/playbook's qualifying body close through the far edge. If studying BPR, confirm overlap of a bullish and bearish FVG.
Record wick touch, partial fill, full fill and invalidation separately. Do not mix a two-candle body imbalance with a three-candle FVG.
tutorials.deliverable: Ten candidate zones with candle OHLC, calculated boundaries/midpoint, mitigation state and at least two rejected/non-qualifying examples.
review: Three-candle boundaries are correct.
CE is calculated from the selected zone edges.
Wick touch and body-close invalidation are not conflated.
tutorials.sourceNotes: Practice workflow based on the playbook; completion is educational practice, not evidence of strategy performance.

tutorials.title: Map Dealing Range, Premium/Discount and PD Arrays
tutorials.objective: Anchor one dealing range to a structural event, calculate equilibrium and map reference arrays without redrawing anchors.
materials: A completed chart with a clearly identified structural leg
A fixed swing-high/swing-low selection rule
A calculator or Fibonacci tool
steps: Identify the structural event that defines the range. Record timeframe, anchor high and anchor low before examining subsequent price action.
Calculate equilibrium as the arithmetic midpoint between the two chosen range extremes. Label above and below only after the range is fixed.
Mark relevant PD Arrays inside or around the range, such as FVGs, order blocks or breakers, and state the boundary convention used.
If using OTE or extensions, record the exact impulse anchors and the percentage convention. Treat these as practitioner references rather than statistical probabilities.
Record what would invalidate the range or array and when a new structural event is allowed to create a replacement range.
tutorials.deliverable: Five fixed dealing-range maps with the anchors, midpoint, premium/discount, arrays and invalidation rules visible.
review: Range anchors are justified by a structural event.
Equilibrium is exactly 50% of the selected range.
The range is not moved after the outcome is visible.
tutorials.sourceNotes: Practice workflow based on the playbook; completion is educational practice, not evidence of strategy performance.

tutorials.title: Build a DST-Safe Session and Time-Anchor Plan
tutorials.objective: Apply session windows and time anchors using America/New_York and the correct exchange schedule.
materials: A timezone-aware chart or clock
The instrument's official trading-hours calendar
A completed chart spanning a DST change
steps: Set the reference timezone to America/New_York. Do not hard-code one IST offset for the whole year.
Verify the product session, maintenance break and holiday schedule on the official exchange source.
Mark the playbook's chosen session or anchor window only after writing down its start/end definition.
Carry the completed range high/low or open reference forward and record whether price rejects or accepts beyond it.
Keep a time window separate from direction: a killzone or Silver Bullet window does not create a setup without the required location and trigger.
tutorials.deliverable: A weekly session sheet in ET and converted IST with DST notes, product session source and three annotated completed sessions.
review: America/New_York is used as the reference zone.
IST conversions change with US DST.
Exchange open, ICT midnight open and broker day open remain distinct.
tutorials.sourceNotes: Practice workflow based on the playbook; completion is educational practice, not evidence of strategy performance.

tutorials.title: Run a Cross-Market SMT Comparison
tutorials.objective: Compare related futures markets on synchronized swings and matched expiries, while treating SMT as a filter rather than a standalone trigger.
materials: Two or three related contracts with matched expiry conventions
Synchronized chart timezones and sessions
A dated comparison log
steps: Choose the pair/group in advance (for example NQ/ES/YM, 6E/6B/DX or GC/SI) and state whether the comparison is direct or inverse.
Match the session, swing timestamps and contract-expiry basis. Do not compare mismatched continuous-contract rolls.
Mark the same prior swing/reference on each market and record which market confirms or fails to confirm.
Label a divergence candidate only when the swing comparison is genuinely comparable. Check market-specific news or contract differences.
Wait for the execution market's own structure/trigger rule; do not enter solely because another market failed to make a new high/low.
tutorials.deliverable: Ten synchronized comparison examples, including confirming and non-confirming cases, with a separate trigger/invalidation field.
review: Same time window and expiry basis are used.
Inverse comparisons are handled explicitly.
SMT is not treated as a standalone entry signal.
tutorials.sourceNotes: Practice workflow based on the playbook; completion is educational practice, not evidence of strategy performance.

tutorials.title: Replay an Entry Model Without Hindsight
tutorials.objective: Convert an ICT model into a checklist of context, trigger, entry, invalidation, target and no-trade conditions.
materials: One model definition from the supplied playbook
A completed replay chart and exact contract/timeframe
Risk calculator and trade journal
steps: Choose exactly one model and copy its prerequisites into a checklist before replay.
Mark the higher-timeframe context, relevant liquidity and session/time conditions before exposing the later candles.
Walk forward one bar at a time. Mark each prerequisite as pass, fail or unavailable. A missing requirement means the model is not qualified.
Only after qualification, write the exact entry, stop/invalidation, target and size assumptions. Include commission, fees and slippage in any later performance study.
Log both qualified and disqualified cases. Do not report win rate or expectancy from a hand-picked sample.
tutorials.deliverable: A 20-case model replay ledger with qualified/no-trade labels, rule version, costs assumption and screenshots.
review: All prerequisites are defined before replay.
No hindsight relabeling of the setup.
No performance claim without a reproducible test.
tutorials.sourceNotes: Practice workflow based on the playbook; completion is educational practice, not evidence of strategy performance.

tutorials.title: Audit a Supplemental ICT/SMC Term
tutorials.objective: Research non-standard terminology without elevating community labels into canonical ICT rules.
materials: The existing source note and references for a selected concept
At least two source descriptions when available
A rule-definition sheet
steps: Start with the concept's evidence label and source note. Identify whether it is source-derived, supplemental, secondary or community terminology.
Open each cited source and record its author, date, wording and exact boundary/trigger definition. Do not treat search results as official lesson verification.
Compare definitions and list any disagreement. If no primary definition is available, retain the item as a research glossary note.
Write a measurable operational version with timeframe, price boundary, close/wick condition and invalidation—or mark it as not yet operational.
Only after the definition is stable should you collect examples for replay. Keep versions separate when source rules differ.
tutorials.deliverable: A source-comparison note with at least two reference entries where available, rule variants, uncertainty statement and a not-to-trade-until-defined decision.
review: Primary and secondary sources are distinguished.
Definition variants are preserved, not blended.
No unverified term is presented as an official signal.

sourceDocument.title: ICT Futures Playbook Complete Edition
sourceDocument.provenanceNote: The playbook is a secondary synthesis. evidenceLabels.SOURCED: Named source and exact claim recorded; prefer primary exchange/regulator for contract facts.
evidenceLabels.CONVENTION: Community practice/editorial synthesis; not a deterministic or statistically tested rule.
evidenceLabels.NO DATA: Independently audited public performance evidence not located; absence of evidence is not proof of no edge.
evidenceLabels.HYPOTHESIS: A testable proposed interpretation, not an established fact.
evidenceLabels.TESTED: Only when a reproducible test links dataset, dates, costs, rules, sample size and out-of-sample results.

playbookTraceability.note: Monthly/Weekly/Daily context; 4H/1H setup; 15M confirmation; 5M/1M entry is the PDF framework, not a universal rule.
T1/T2/T3 are the PDF's study tiers, not objective rankings. Sourced pair examples: NQ–ES–YM; 6E–6B–DX inverse comparison; GC–SI. Other comparisons are convention. Match expiry.
Bias → target → confirmation → entry zone → range filter → time; liquidity and sweep definitions remain framework-dependent.

playbookTraceability.section: FVG, order blocks and PD arrays
playbookTraceability.note: Wick/close, mitigation and boundary variants must be explicit. FPFVG and some blocks are convention/supplemental terms.

playbookTraceability.section: Time anchors, narratives, weekly profiles and SMT
playbookTraceability.note: Session windows need timezone/DST verification. Source-described ideas must be separated from community synthesis.
The PDF does not establish a best ICT model through audited public performance statistics; spot-gold/BTC examples are not futures proof.

playbookTraceability.section: Sessions, Globex, expiry/roll and event calendar
playbookTraceability.note: December 2026 roll dates and 2026 event dates are examples only. Product-specific exchange hours and holiday/DST exceptions apply.
The PDF warns some FX tick values vary and omits margin because it changes; its sample calculations are educational, not current specs.
Use contract/window, risk, news and expiry fields in the trade-plan and replay workbook.
Glossary terms map to existing concepts or the six new foundations lessons. PDF research limitations remain visible.
